witness.method: REPAIR of prior VERIFIER_FAIL: the previous scan only certified via primes p>k, which is unsound when the bound min(n-k+1, k^(1+c)) drops to <= k (it equals n-k+1 there, for k >= (n+1)/2), since P(C(n,k)) may then be a prime <= k. Repair: (fast path) descending scan over primes p>k with an exact window criterion for divisibility of C(n,k) — v_p(C)=#multiples of p in (n-k,n] is exact because p>k forces p∤k!; a hit with p>=bound passes. (fallback, always exact and complete) if the fast path cannot certify, compute v_p(C(n,k)) exactly for EVERY prime p<=n via Legendre's formula v_p(n!)-v_p(k!)-v_p((n-k)!), take the true largest prime factor, and compare to the bound in exact integers (x >= k^(1+c) <=> x^b >= k^(b+a) for c=a/b). Any unresolved case raises (fail-closed). k=n: P(1)=1 vs bound min(1,...)=1, exact. k=1: P(n) by trial division <= 3000, exact.

claim: verify() == True (any violation raises) establishes lemma L1's exact finite core: for every 1<=k<=n<=3000 and every c in {1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1}, P(C(n,k)) >= min(n-k+1, k^(1+c)) — with P(1):=1 at k=n — certified by exact integer arithmetic (fast prime-window path for p>k, complete Legendre-valuation fallback covering primes <= k so no case is decided by an unsound shortcut), fail-closed, no floats, no I/O. covers="fragment": certifies the finite grid only; the ∀c>0 extension and the branch-B close are explicitly outside certificate scope, as L1 itself states.
law: Wang 7.2: an exact finite object plus a proved reduction is a CERTIFICATE. The reduction is the `claim` and is a human's to audit; the object and the verifier run are the machine's part.
